::: {.why}
The failure modes are opposite and both common: describing genetics work in its own vocabulary so nobody reads it, or dressing it up as finance so a researcher stops trusting you in the second line.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Rewrite the research section in the language of the job without misdescribing what you did.
- Have every line on the first page either state a measurable result or a technique the reader recognises.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Rewrite the research section: Mendelian randomization becomes instrumental variable estimation with weak-instrument diagnostics, a genome-wide scan becomes high-dimensional multiple testing with a controlled error rate, and colocalization becomes Bayesian model comparison over shared causal variants. Each of those is true and each is a technique the reader uses.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Add this year's work with numbers rather than nouns: the platform with its test suite, the alpha book with its specification count, the audit with its interval, and the paper-traded track record with its length. Then cut everything from the first page that is neither a result nor a recognised technique.
:::
:::

## Deliverable

::: {.deliverable}
A rewritten CV whose first page contains only measurable results and recognised techniques.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
Describe your thesis work in the vocabulary of quantitative research, in three sentences, without overclaiming.
:::
